title: 11. Projects: File Handling
summary: These mini-projects will help you apply file handling concepts in real-world scenarios. Each project focuses on different aspects of file operations and data processing.
objectives: Build the File Handling projects end to end

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: These mini-projects will help you apply file handling concepts in real-world scenarios. Each project focuses on different aspects of file operations and data processing.

sections.title: Project 1: Text File Analyzer
sections.body:
### 🎯 Learning Objectives
- Master basic file reading and writing operations
- Implement text analysis algorithms
- Handle file encoding and error scenarios
- Process large files efficiently

### 📋 Project Description
Create a comprehensive text file analyzer that can process any text file and provide detailed statistics and analysis.

### 🗂️ Data Structure
```
Input: Any text file (.txt, .md, .py, etc.)
Output: Analysis report with statistics
```

### 🔧 Implementation Tasks
1. **File Reader Module**
   - Read files with proper encoding detection
   - Handle different file sizes (small to large)
   - Implement error handling for missing files

2. **Text Analysis Engine**
   - Count characters, words, lines, and paragraphs
   - Find the longest and shortest lines
   - Calculate average word length
   - Identify most common words

3. **Statistics Generator**
   - Generate reading time estimates
   - Calculate text complexity metrics
   - Create word frequency distribution

4. **Report Generator**
   - Create formatted analysis reports
   - Export results to different formats (TXT, CSV, JSON)
   - Generate visual summaries

### 💡 Hints
- Use context managers for safe file operations
- Process large files line by line to save memory
- Consider using regular expressions for advanced text analysis
- Implement progress indicators for large files

### 📊 Expected Output
```
Text File Analysis Report
========================
File: sample.txt
Size: 1,234 bytes
Lines: 45
Words: 234
Characters: 1,567

Reading Statistics:
- Estimated reading time: 2 minutes
- Average words per line: 5.2
- Longest line: 78 characters
- Shortest line: 3 characters

Word Analysis:
- Most common word: "the" (15 occurrences)
- Average word length: 4.8 characters
- Unique words: 156

Complexity Metrics:
- Flesch Reading Ease: 65.2
- Text complexity: Medium
```

sections.title: Project 2: CSV Data Processor
sections.body:
### 🎯 Learning Objectives
- Work with structured data formats
- Implement data validation and cleaning
- Handle CSV parsing and generation
- Create data transformation pipelines

### 📋 Project Description
Build a CSV data processor that can read, validate, clean, and transform CSV files with various data types and formats.

### 🗂️ Data Structure
```
Input: CSV files with various schemas
Output: Cleaned and processed CSV files
```

### 🔧 Implementation Tasks
1. **CSV Reader and Validator**
   - Detect CSV format and delimiter
   - Validate data types for each column
   - Identify missing or malformed data
   - Generate data quality reports

2. **Data Cleaning Engine**
   - Remove duplicate rows
   - Handle missing values (fill, drop, or interpolate)
   - Standardize data formats (dates, numbers, text)
   - Remove outliers based on statistical methods

3. **Data Transformation Module**
   - Convert data types (string to number, date parsing)
   - Create calculated columns
   - Aggregate data by groups
   - Filter data based on conditions

4. **Export and Reporting**
   - Export cleaned data to new CSV files
   - Generate data quality reports
   - Create summary statistics
   - Support multiple output formats

### 💡 Hints
- Use pandas for complex data operations
- Implement configurable cleaning rules
- Handle different date and number formats
- Create backup files before processing

### 📊 Expected Output
```
CSV Data Processing Report
=========================
Input File: sales_data.csv
Records Processed: 1,000
Records Cleaned: 1,000
Records Removed: 15

Data Quality Issues Found:
- Missing values: 23
- Duplicate records: 8
- Invalid dates: 5
- Outliers: 12

Cleaning Actions:
- Filled missing values: 18
- Removed duplicates: 8
- Standardized dates: 5
- Removed outliers: 12

Output File: sales_data_cleaned.csv
Processing Time: 2.3 seconds
```

sections.title: Project 3: Log File Monitor
sections.body:
### 🎯 Learning Objectives
- Process real-time log files
- Implement log parsing and analysis
- Create monitoring and alerting systems
- Handle different log formats

### 📋 Project Description
Develop a log file monitoring system that can track, analyze, and alert on log file changes in real-time.

### 🗂️ Data Structure
```
Input: Various log file formats (Apache, Nginx, application logs)
Output: Real-time alerts and analysis reports
```

### 🔧 Implementation Tasks
1. **Log File Watcher**
   - Monitor log files for changes
   - Handle log rotation
   - Support multiple log files simultaneously
   - Implement file change detection

2. **Log Parser Engine**
   - Parse different log formats
   - Extract timestamps, log levels, and messages
   - Handle structured and unstructured logs
   - Support custom log formats

3. **Analysis and Alerting**
   - Count log entries by level (INFO, WARNING, ERROR)
   - Detect error patterns and anomalies
   - Generate real-time alerts
   - Create trend analysis

4. **Reporting Dashboard**
   - Generate hourly/daily summaries
   - Create visual reports
   - Export analysis data
   - Maintain historical data

### 💡 Hints
- Use file system monitoring libraries
- Implement configurable parsing rules
- Handle large log files efficiently
- Create alert thresholds and rules

### 📊 Expected Output
```

==================================
```

sections.title: Project 4: Configuration File Manager
sections.body:
### 🎯 Learning Objectives
- Work with different configuration file formats
- Implement configuration validation
- Create backup and version control systems
- Handle environment-specific configurations

### 📋 Project Description
Build a configuration file manager that can handle multiple file formats, validate configurations, and manage different environments.

### 🗂️ Data Structure
```
Input: Configuration files (INI, JSON, YAML, ENV)
Output: Validated and managed configuration files
```

### 🔧 Implementation Tasks
1. **Configuration Parser**
   - Support multiple file formats (INI, JSON, YAML, ENV)
   - Parse and validate configuration syntax
   - Handle nested configurations
   - Support environment variable substitution

2. **Validation Engine**
   - Validate configuration values
   - Check required fields
   - Verify data types and ranges
   - Generate validation reports

3. **Configuration Manager**
   - Create configuration backups
   - Manage different environments (dev, staging, prod)
   - Implement configuration versioning
   - Handle sensitive data encryption

4. **Deployment Tools**
   - Generate environment-specific configs
   - Create configuration templates
   - Implement rollback functionality
   - Support configuration inheritance

### 💡 Hints
- Use appropriate libraries for each file format
- Implement schema validation for configurations
- Create secure handling of sensitive data
- Use environment variables for dynamic values

### 📊 Expected Output
```
Configuration Manager Report
============================

- Staging: config.staging.json ✓

- Dependencies: All satisfied

Security Check:

- Access permissions: Secure
- Backup integrity: Verified

Deployment Status:

- Environment configs: Updated
- Rollback points: Created
```

sections.title: Project 5: File Synchronization Tool
sections.body:
### 🎯 Learning Objectives
- Implement file comparison algorithms
- Handle file synchronization across directories
- Manage file conflicts and resolution
- Create backup and recovery systems

### 📋 Project Description
Create a file synchronization tool that can compare directories, detect changes, and synchronize files between different locations.

### 🗂️ Data Structure
```
Input: Source and destination directories
Output: Synchronized directories with conflict resolution
```

### 🔧 Implementation Tasks
1. **File Scanner and Indexer**
   - Scan directories recursively
   - Create file indexes with metadata
   - Calculate file hashes for comparison
   - Handle different file types

2. **Change Detection Engine**
   - Compare file contents and metadata
   - Detect new, modified, and deleted files
   - Handle file conflicts
   - Generate change reports

3. **Synchronization Engine**
   - Copy new and modified files
   - Remove deleted files
   - Handle file conflicts
   - Maintain directory structure

4. **Backup and Recovery**
   - Create backup before synchronization
   - Implement rollback functionality
   - Handle synchronization failures
   - Maintain synchronization logs

### 💡 Hints
- Use file hashing for efficient comparison
- Implement incremental synchronization
- Handle large files and directories
- Create conflict resolution strategies

sections.title: Project Implementation Tips
sections.body:
### 📝 Planning Phase
1. **Requirements Analysis**
   - Define clear project objectives
   - Identify input/output formats
   - Plan error handling strategies
   - Design user interface (if needed)

2. **Architecture Design**
   - Break down into modules
   - Define data structures
   - Plan file organization
   - Consider scalability

3. **Testing Strategy**
   - Create test data sets
   - Plan unit and integration tests
   - Design error scenarios
   - Prepare validation criteria

### 🔧 Development Phase
1. **Start Simple**
   - Begin with basic functionality
   - Add features incrementally
   - Test each component thoroughly
   - Document your code

2. **Error Handling**
   - Implement comprehensive error handling
   - Create meaningful error messages
   - Add logging for debugging
   - Plan recovery mechanisms

3. **Performance Optimization**
   - Profile your code
   - Optimize file operations
   - Handle large files efficiently
   - Consider memory usage

### 📊 Testing and Validation
1. **Functional Testing**
   - Test with various file types
   - Verify all features work correctly
   - Test edge cases and error conditions
   - Validate output formats

2. **Performance Testing**
   - Test with large files
   - Measure processing times
   - Check memory usage
   - Optimize bottlenecks

3. **User Acceptance**
   - Test with real-world data
   - Gather feedback
   - Refine user experience
   - Document usage instructions

### 🎯 Success Criteria
- All core functionality works correctly
- Error handling is robust
- Performance is acceptable
- Code is well-documented
- User interface is intuitive (if applicable)
- Project can handle real-world scenarios

Remember: These projects are designed to challenge you and help you master file handling concepts. Take your time, plan carefully, and don't hesitate to iterate and improve your solutions!
